# pdf20-hash cases

Read by `tests/oracle/aes.test.ts` (Algorithm 2.B, ISO 32000-2 7.6.4.3.4). Never edit `cases.json` by hand.

- Generated by qpdf version 12.4.2 with `node scripts/oracle/pdf20-hash-cases.ts`, which runs `qpdf --empty --encrypt --user-password=<user> --owner-password=<owner> --bits=256 -- <out>` once for each of 256 seeded password pairs and records the R6 Encrypt dictionary of each file (`/P`, `/U`, `/O`, `/UE`, `/OE`, `/Perms`, strings as lower-case hex).
- Each file gives two cases, 512 in all: the user password with the salt in bytes 32-39 of `/U`, whose hash is bytes 0-31 of `/U`; and the owner password with the salt in bytes 32-39 of `/O` and the 48-byte `/U` as udata, whose hash is bytes 0-31 of `/O`.
- User passwords are 0 to 127 bytes of printable ASCII (every eighth one empty); owner passwords are 1 to 127 bytes and never equal to the user password.

The passwords come from a seeded generator and are the same on every run, but qpdf draws the salts at random, so a new run writes different hashes. Verify with `node scripts/oracle/pdf20-hash-cases.ts --check`: it checks the passwords and the shape of the file, rebuilds each empty document from its committed Encrypt dictionary and requires qpdf `--show-encryption` to report the user password as the user password and the owner password as the owner password. Both modes need qpdf 12.4.2 (`QPDF=<path>` or `qpdf` on PATH) and refuse any other version.

These are test data only: the passwords are public.
